analysis: Both units are head-side excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 5074-6861). They hold public synthetic test vectors for the prompt-contract/prefix-cache logic: request_body, provider_body, template_input, plan block-boundary chain hashes, and token_ids. The file_changes patch shows the PR updates the vectors: adds additional_context enable_thinking=false in one case, changes token counts and chain hashes, and adjusts token IDs. Entries seen here (multi_system, nulls, reasoning_effort, response_text) contain only obviously public placeholder text such as "Public followup.", "Nulls must disappear" and "Public synthetic cache-parity input.". No secrets, keys, tokens, credentials or real consumer data are present. The fixture is test data and does not touch authorization, attestation, encryption, or the coordinator/provider wire contract (TB-002, TB-011), so no threat-model assets change. The only relevant surface is T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing), where chain hashes and prompt_contract_id are cache-key inputs; the fixture is public and the hashes are derived from public text. Limits: the patch excerpt is truncated and the producing/consuming Swift or Go code is not supplied. I could not verify that the new vectors match the implementation, or whether an unseen implementation change (for example, how enable_thinking affects template rendering or cache keying) has a cache-isolation impact. Also, the prompt_contract_id is unchanged (8171fec3...) while template inputs and token output changed for the enable_thinking case. That could be a versioning concern for cache-key separation, but it is not provable from the supplied evidence. Integration should check that any template-behaviour change is reflected in the contract ID used for cache namespace separation.
